auxiliary_material: The review highlights tumor-type heterogeneity, noting that across all solid tumors except hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), antibiotic exposure was consistently associated with worse OS. In HCC, the association depended on hepatitis infection status. A large melanoma cohort did not demonstrate a significant association. The authors suggest clinicians consider delaying ICI initiation for 30–60 days following recent antibiotic exposure when clinically appropriate, though this is based on retrospective data. The search strategy was limited to human studies published in English within the last 10 years.
outline_action: Use this study to support the general consensus that antibiotic exposure negatively impacts ICI efficacy (broad-spectrum effect) and to cite the emerging signal that fluoroquinolones may carry higher risk than other classes. Explicitly note the review's conclusion that class-specific effects require further definition to avoid overstating the safety of non-fluoroquinolone classes. Include the tumor-type exceptions (melanoma, HCC) when discussing the heterogeneity of the microbiome-ICI axis. If possible, locate the original primary studies referenced within this review that performed the class-specific comparisons to meet the '2 studies' success criterion more robustly.
remaining_gap: While this review indicates potential class-specific effects (fluoroquinolones potentially having a worse impact), it explicitly states that further prospective studies are needed to define these effects, meaning the evidence is not yet definitive enough to confirm which specific classes are 'relatively safe'. The success criterion requires finding at least 2 studies comparing classes or stating only broad-spectrum effects are supported; this material summarizes multiple studies but concludes the class-specific data is not fully defined, leaving the question of specific safe classes partially unresolved.
useful_material: This study is a systematic review of 25 studies comprising approximately 73,567 patients with solid tumors treated with ICIs. It found that antibiotic exposure within 30–60 days before or during ICI therapy was associated with inferior overall survival (OS) in the majority of studies (22 of 25), with hazard ratios ranging from 1.08 to 2.55. Regarding antibiotic classes, the authors reported that several included studies suggested outcomes varied by class, specifically noting fluoroquinolones were associated with worse survival compared with other antibiotic classes in select analyses. However, the review concluded that further prospective studies are needed to define class-specific antibiotic effects. The study also noted exceptions where the association was not significant (melanoma) or variable (hepatocellular carcinoma dependent on hepatitis infection status).
